articleTitle: Subterahertz and mid IR spectroscopy of explosive substances
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: The present work reports on detection of explosives substances (NG, TNT, RDX) in subTHz and midIR, based on registration of certain marker-molecules evaporated from surfaces of samples. Experimental results of both methods are in good agreement and have demonstrated a presence of nitric oxides, ammonia, acetone, etc in explosives vapors.

articleTitle: The AILES beamline for THz and IR spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: The new infrared beamline (AILES) at the third generation Synchrotron Radiation source SOLEIL is now available for users. This beamline exploits infrared and THz synchrotron radiation from both edge emission and the constant field conventional source. The performances including flux, spatial distribution of the photons, spectral range and stability are discussed and the optical system and spectroscopic stations are described. The combined source with the adapted optics of the beamline offers high flux and brilliance for all kinds of infrared experiments. We will briefly review the main research themes and future developments of coherent emission at SOLEIL.

articleTitle: Orotron oscillators and frequency multipliers as sources of coherent terahertz radiation
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: The orotron (the Smith-Purcell electron microwave tube with open cavity) provides coherent radiation at the frequencies up to 0.4 THz. The output power of 50-100 mW is obtained in the microsecond pulses with possibility of a wide frequency tuning. A proposed new scheme of a frequency-multiplication regime allows increasing the orotron operating frequency up to 0.6 THz.

articleTitle: Is the stimulated emission of THz photons feasible at the inverse population of lattice vibration states?
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: Stimulated emission of THz electromagnetic waves related to the phonon-difference processes are discussed supposing the lattice vibration states to be populated inversely to their thermal equilibrium. Numerical data are presented for zincblende GaN.

articleTitle: Recent advances in infrared semiconductor based chemical sensing technologies
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: Recent advances in the development of sensors based on the use of quantum cascade lasers (QCLs) for the sensitive, selective detection, quantification and monitoring of both small and large molecular gas species with resolved and unresolved spectroscopic features respectively will be reported.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic wave diffraction by a doubly-periodic grating of uninterrupted curvilinear metal strips placed on both surfaces of a dielectric layer
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: The problem of electromagnetic wave scattering by a planar doubly-layer structure (DLS) consisting of doubly-periodic strip gratings placed on both surfaces of a dielectric layer are solved using a numerical method. The influence of the strip shift in neighboring layers on diffraction characteristics is analyzed. The frequency dependence of surface current values on the structure Strips is considered in the case of a small distance between layers.

articleTitle: Development of (λ∼9.4µm) GaAs-based quantum cascade lasers
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: The development of (λ∼9.4µm) GaAs-based quantum cascade lasers (QCLs) operating over 260K is reported. The laser design followed an “anticrossed-diagonal” scheme of Page et al. [1]. The QCL GaAs/Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.45</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.55</inf>As heterostructures were grown by solid source (SS) MBE. The double trench lasers were fabricated using wet etching and Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> for electrical insulation. Double plasmon confinement with Al-free waveguide has been used to minimize absorption losses. Optical and electrical properties of resulting devices are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: All-optical amplitude modulation of a middle-infrared quantum cascade laser
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: We demonstrated the all-optical modulation in the optical emission power of a standard middle infrared quantum cascade laser by optically illuminating its front facet with femtosecond near infrared pulse train. The modulation frequency is found up to 10.35 GHz, much faster than the observed laser current response, only 3 GHz.

articleTitle: Electron-beam lithographed metamaterial devices operating in the terahertz region
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: Direct electron-beam lithography (EBL) was exploited to fabricate metamaterial devices operating in the terahertz (THz) region. Simulation show that, in order to reach the required frequency range, optimized metallic structures deposited on silicon must have submicron features. The effect of an external parameter, such as the substrate doping, is also studied.

articleTitle: 3D protein structure determination by THz spectroscopy and molecular modelling: case study on bovine serum albumin
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: THz spectroscopy is a very powerful tool in investigating the vibrational modes and conformational transitions of biomolecules. Here we have used THz spectroscopy to study the vibrational spectrum of bovine serum albumin, a protein whose 3D structure is yet unknown. Experimental data were fitted with theoretical spectra obtained by normal modes analysis of BSA structures generated by homology modeling.

articleTitle: Optical spectral characteristics modeling for nitride quantum-cascade detectors
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: We present the theoretical analysis of resonance quantum cascade photodetector based on GaN/AlGaN compound. Calculation of reflection, transmission spectra and optical quantum efficiency was made by semianalytical methodic.

articleTitle: Nanosecond pulses for sub-terahertz imaging from avalanching GaAs bipolar transistors
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: We present direct experimental observation of sub-terahertz emission in milliwatt-range nanosecond pulses obtained from miniature GaAs bipolar transistor chips at room temperature. The emission is attributed to the recently introduced ¿collapsing¿ field domains. This new emitter combined with the high-speed bolometers used in measurements could provide a means for developing unique sub-terahertz imagers.

articleTitle: Design of high-energy THz sources based on optical rectification
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: Different materials suitable for optical rectification are compared in terms of maximal THz generation efficiency and the spectral content. Semiconductors can be advantageous for generating higher-frequency THz pulses; however, the relative spectral width is typically smaller than that in LiNbO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>. Furthermore, it is shown that imaging errors in the tilted-pulse-front pumping scheme can lead to a THz beam with strong divergence and asymmetric intensity profile, thereby limiting applications. Optimized setup parameters were found to reduce such distortions.

articleTitle: Coherent superposition of terahertz beams from a phased linear photomixer array
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: We report on a 4 element linear array of free standing, tunable THz n-i-pn-i-p superlattice photomixers. The individual THz beams are coherently combined at a target plane distance of 4.2 m. The measurements of the interference pattern confirm the theoretically expected quadratic intensity increase of the center beam with the number of sources. At the same time, the beam waist is reduced in one dimension by a factor of 6 compared to a single beam. This technique allows for high resolution, THz stand off imaging.

articleTitle: Terahertz active media on intra-center transitions: tuning by nano-layers
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: We show that impurity spectra in delta-doped semiconductor structures can be tailored using a system of wells and barriers with the width smaller than localization radii of impurity states (typically few nanometers). It is expected that optimization of intra-center relaxation in such structures will lead to significant reduction of generation threshold of silicon impurity lasers.

articleTitle: Plasmon resonances in a gated two-dimensional electron system with lateral contacts
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: It is shown that plasmon resonances can be effectively excited in the totally screened two-dimensional electron gas channel with lateral contacts at terahertz frequencies. The linewidth of the plasmon resonance in the totally screened two-dimensional electron gas with lateral contacts shrinks down to the electron scattering contribution, which is the minimal theoretical value for the plasmon resonance linewidth.

articleTitle: Influence of the spot size of the probe beam on the detected THz power using electro-optic detection method
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: We compared the detected THz power through electro-optic detection for different spot sizes of a probe beam on the ¿110¿ ZnTe crystal. We find that there is a proportional relationship between the detected THz power and spot size of the probe beam by theoretically analyzing its effect on the intensity profile of the terahertz beam.

articleTitle: Investigating the glass transition of polymers with terahertz time-domain spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: The glass transition temperature Tg of polymers is identified by terahertz (THz) time-domain spectroscopy (TDS). The THz refractive index n of the investigated material changes significantly in the region of the glass transition. Hence, THz TDS offers the possibility for non-contact polymer analysis.

articleTitle: Interperiods electron transport coherences in quantum-cascade structures
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: Results of electron transport investigation in the quantum-cascade structures are reported. Mathematical model connecting optical characteristic and electron transport have been developed by us applying the density matrix theory. It is shown that series of electron coherent transitions in the injector leads to coherent coupling of adjacent active regions. Such an interperiod coherence becomes apparent as changes in frequency and amplitude of oscillations of observables at the fetmosecond scale.

articleTitle: Reactive ion beam etching of superconducting Bi2212 by Ta/PR and PR'/Ta/PR masks for the generation of THz waves
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: Generation of powerful THz radiation from intrinsic Josephson Junctions (IJJs) of Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Sr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>CaCu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8+¿</sub> (Bi2212) may require mesas with large lateral dimension. However, there are difficulties in fabrication of perfect rectangular mesas. Mesa lateral angles should be close to 90 degrees to obtain IJJs with same planar dimensions for synchronization of IJJs. Since thick photoresist (PR) layer shades the lateral dimension of mesa during ion beam etching, we patterned Ta/PR and PR'/Ta/PR masks on Bi2212 and used selective ion etching to overcome this problem. The reactive ion beam etchings have done with ion beam of Ar, N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and we have obtained mesas about 1 ¿m with lateral angle of approximately 50 to 75° which is better than the mesas fabricated with single layer mask.

articleTitle: Creation of the cavity of the tunable whispering gallery modes mid infrared laser
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: The technology of fabrication disk cavity of whispering gallery modes (WGM) laser for middle Infrared (MIR) spectral range was developed. The post-growth geometry formation of the disk cavity was performed using selective wet chemical etchant comprised of CrO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>, HF and H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O. The wet-chemical etchant for semiconductor multilayers heterostructures lattice-matched to GaSb was investigated. The application of this technology allow us to fabricate the disk cavity with a diameter of 200 ¿m and height 15 ¿m. To enlarge the optical power of emission the disk chip was cleaved up to symmetric half-disk. It was established, that the lasers assembled on the basis of such half-disk cavity are tunable and generate at the wavelength of 2.35 ¿m at 300 K.

articleTitle: Porous InP membranes filled in with monomer composite for terahertz applications
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: Porous n-InP membranes with (111) crystallographic orientation have been filled in with Zn(C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>N0<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>0H)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> monomer. Experimental study and imulations based on FEMs (Finite Element Model) show that the obtained nanocomposite material is promising for nonlinear optical applications, in particular for the development of Terahertz emitters.

articleTitle: Spin polarized tunneling in large area mesas of superconducting Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+δ for the generation of the THz waves
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: Rectangular intrinsic Josephson junction mesa structures of superconducting Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Sr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>CaCu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8+Δ</sub> (Bi2212) can be used as a source of continuous, coherent and polarized terahertz (THz) radiation. THz emitting mesas are below a certain underdoped level of Bi2212. They have small Josephson critical current in contrast to optimally doped and overdoped Bi2212. We deposited Au/Co/Au multilayer top of mesa and obtained small critical current from mesas fabricated by as-grown Bi2212 single crystals due to injection of spin polarized current. The spin injection eliminates adjustment of doping level for successful THz emission.

articleTitle: Clinotrons as powerful sources of terahertz radiation
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: A series of clinotron tubes and clinotron based oscillators, which effectively operate throughout millimeter and sub-millimeter wavelength bands, have been developed at the Institute of Radio Astronomy. In this paper, the design and characteristics of these devices are discussed. Potentials of the clinotron for further upgrading efficiency, output power, and operating frequency are considered as well.

articleTitle: Advancing of methods and technique of mm wavelength range to THz frequency range
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: The present paper reports on elaboration of new THz synthesizers, generators and spectrometers with using of quantum semiconductor superlattice multipliers and mixers.

articleTitle: Double-barrier superlattice infrared photodetector combined with quantum well infrared photodetector for operation at high temperature and low bias
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: We have designed a double-barrier superlattice infrared photodetector combined with quantum well infrared photodetector which has a superlattice (SL) sandwiched between the thick and graded barriers then multiple quantum wells(MQWs) are inserted in the right side of them . The two barriers can let the photoelectrons to bounce back and forth then the photoelectrons inject through the MQWs which are used as noise filter. The detector shows high-temperature operation (~110 K) at low bias. The associated detectivity is also optimized so this device is the promising candidate of a pixel in the focal plane array.

articleTitle: Lifetimes of operating states in terahertz intracenter silicon lasers
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: The result on theoretical and experimental study of principal states relaxation for terahertz range silicon laser based on phosphor and arsenic shallow donor centers are reported. Numerical simulations show that f-TA and f-LA intervalley phonons scattering dominates in laser state relaxation. The theoretical values of relaxation rates fit well to the experimental data obtained by the pump-and-probe modulated transmission technique.

articleTitle: Generation of a narrow linewidth mm-wave signal from two phase-locked DFB lasers that are mutually coupled via Four Wave Mixing
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: Two DFB lasers emitting at different wavelengths are phase-locked via mutual injection assisted by a Four-Wave-Mixing process that takes place in a third auxiliary DFB. This demonstrates the generation of a spectrally pure tunable mm-wave signal without a reference RF seed.

articleTitle: Recent performance records for mid-IR quantum cascade lasers
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: The wall plug efficiency of the mid-infrared quantum cascade laser in room temperature continuous wave operation is brought to 17%. Peak output power from a broad area (400 ¿m × 3 mm) device gives 120 W output power in pulsed mode operation at room temperature. Using a single-well-injector design, specifically made for low temperature operation, a record wall plug efficiency of 53% is demonstrated at 40 K.

articleTitle: Telecom-wavelength compatible THz n-i-pn-i-p superlattice photomixers for spectroscopical applications
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: We report on the progress of room-temperature operating, continuous-wave, tunable n-i-pn-i-p superlattice THz photomixers, compatible with 1.55 ¿m telecom laser systems. An output power of 0.2 ¿W at 1 THz has been achieved at a photocurrent of 9.4 mA, using a broadband antenna. The spectral power is at a level where high resolution spectroscopy becomes attractive. This is demonstrated by measuring the absorption spectrum of water vapor between 0.4 and 1.6 THz.

articleTitle: Experimental modeling the passive devices, based on surface oscillations for the THz-GHz band
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: The experimental research of principles of development and design passive elements for canalization of electromagnetic energy, based on possibility of control the effective constitutive parameters of the composite media where the wave propagates are under consideration.

articleTitle: Microwave features of optic photonic crystals
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: Dispersion of nonresonant electromagnetic waves of millimeter waveband absorption in structures based on opal matrix with imbedded magnetic impurities has been experimentally investigated. The method of constitutive parameters definition for structures which demonstrate photonic crystal features in visible and IR wavebands has been proposed.

articleTitle: Left-handed properties of composite ferrite/semiconductor medium oriented in staggered order
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: The work is devoted to numerical research of properties of left-handed medium (LHM) formed by ferrite-semiconductor elements oriented in staggered order in millimeter waveband.

articleTitle: Kinetics of shallow acceptor impact ionization and recombination in p-Ge
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: The time evolution of current in p-Ge doped with shallow acceptors was studied. The dependences of impact ionization and recombination times on electric field and uniaxial pressure were found. The role of Poole-Frenkel ionization of shallow acceptors was analyzed.

articleTitle: Highly effective array feed for RATAN-600 radio telescope in a multibeam mode
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: The new optical scheme of RATAN-600 in a multibeam mode a compact effective array feed in 3-8 mm band is described. Two compact smooth-walled spline-profile horns as alternative to the corrugated horn has been optimized, manufactured and tested. The antenna measurement and theoretical results are in good agreement with simulation. The results of the trial observations at the RATAN-600 radio telescope with the suggested horn as a feed are given. The multi-beam receiving array for a radio telescope is calculated.

articleTitle: Challenges for intersubband terahertz emitters and possible solutions through advanced numerical simulations
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: This talk starts with an overview of present challenges for TERA-MIR devices and the state of the art of the most promising device for this range: the quantum cascade laser (QCL). The need for advanced quantum statistical mechanics, many particle and nonequilibrium Physics to describe these devices will be explained and results of our leading edge simulator will be presented. In the last part of the talk progress on intersubband lasing without inversion will be discussed, since those designs can mitigate some of the most crucial problems faced by THz QCLs. In particular the influence of increasing dephasing on the k-space filtering mechanism will be discussed.

articleTitle: High-resolution X-ray characterization of mid-IR QCL structures
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: In this paper, five Quantum Cascade Laser structures were investigated by using high-resolution X-ray diffractometry. The information about perfection and periodicity of the structures was derived from simulation of diffraction profiles generated using dynamical diffraction theory. HRXRD characterization enabled to optimize the growth conditions of the laser structures towards achieving the high degree of crystalline quality necessary for optimum device performance.

articleTitle: Characterization of Air-nitrogen-argon DC glow discharge plasma with THz time domain spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: Transmission of terahertz pulses through DC glow discharge plasma was investigated for different gages. The pressure was kept in between the range of 0.1 torr-0.5 torr and for each pressure different measurements were at 5 mA, 10 mA and 15 mA plasma currents. Moreover, emission spectrum of Air, N<sub>2</sub> and Ar plasma analysis were done respectively. It was found that the transmission of terahertz pulses through nitrogen plasma was considerably affected compared to that of the argon plasma.

articleTitle: Numerical improvement of terahertz time-domain spectroscopic measurements
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: We have developed an algorithm to efficiently eliminate unwanted reflections typically observed in the data obtained by Terahertz time-domain spectroscopic (THz-TDS) methods. The algorithm works by eliminating the reflections from the boundaries. The numerical improvement of the data allows better analysis of the critical parameters obtained by THz-TDS systems.

articleTitle: Electrical injection of intersubband polaritons
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: We study the electro-luminescence spectra of an electrically injected intersubband polariton device. The experimental results show a large tunability of the injected electrons energy. Data are compared to the electro luminescence spectra simulated thanks to the theoretical model described.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave scale metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: We review two metamaterial configurations, which are operating at the millimeter-wave scale, in terms of design, fabrication, and characterization. We observed both numerically and experimentally at around 100 GHz a narrow frequency band for which the metamaterial was low loss and had a negative index of refraction. We investigated flat and wedge shaped samples to support our characterization results. We analyzed the transmission band with respect to number of layers at the propagation direction and commented on the bulk nature of these metamaterials. Oblique response of the planar sample was also included in this study. Finally, we demonstrate a device, which yields a rather small angular width at the far field radiation pattern, and composed of a horn antenna and flat metamaterial slabs at the propagation direction.

articleTitle: Sol-gel synthesis of barium-strontium titanate in porous anodic alumina for uncooled IR detector
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: We report on sol-gel synthesis of barium-strontium titanate (BST) in porous anodic alumina. BST inside the channels of mesoporous matrices is considered as component allowing observation of phase transition under IR irradiation, thus, from our viewpoint, tunable photonic crystal for detection of IR irradiation could be developed. Sol-gel derived BST doped with terbium fabricated in porous anodic alumina exhibits room-temperature Tb-related photoluminescence (PL).

articleTitle: THz waveguide and bends based on metallic photonic crystals
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: Metallic band-gap structures for THz waveguide and bends have been simulated using the finite element method. Transmission characteristics have been obtained for various square array waveguide designs.

articleTitle: Detection of explosive under covering soap using the THz spectral dynamics analysis
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: We demonstrate a high efficiency of a method of THz spectral dynamics analysis (SDA) for a treatment of compound medium response in the THz and GHz ranges for problem of identification of explosive under cover of soap, for example. The response represents a mixture of responses of a soap and explosive in different proportions on action of THz pulse with a few cycles. Such a way we make modeling the response of explosive under covering soap.

articleTitle: Large Amplitude anharmonic vibrations driven by monocycle intense THz pulse
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: Intense monocycle THz pulse can drive large-amplitude vibration mode which gives us a chance to perform novel THz nonlinear spectroscopy. We experimentally demonstrated large amplitude anharmonic intermolecular vibration mode using intense monocycle THz pulse. We performed the nonlinear transmission spectroscopy of the amino acids micro-crystals at different electric field amplitude and observed the nonlinearity of vibration spectrum.

articleTitle: Magnetoplasma waves in semiconductor periodic and quasi-periodic layered waveguides
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: The effect of the external magnetic field on the properties of the eigenwaves of layered periodic and quasi-periodic waveguides composed of alternating layers of dielectric and semiconductor is considered in the work. The dispersion dependencies for finite medium and field distribution are obtained.

articleTitle: Electrical and optical characterisation of (λ∼9.4µm) GaAs-based quantum cascade lasers
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: The basic device characterization of (λ-9.4 μm) GaAs-based quantum cascade lasers (QCLs) operating up to 260 K is reported. The laser design followed an "anticrossed-diagonal" scheme. The QCL structures were grown by MBE, with Riber Compact 21T reactor. The influence of injector doping on electrical and optical properties of the lasers has been clarified.

articleTitle: Density-matrix theory of quantum cascade lasers: Localization effects
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: A density-matrix theory is employed to study dynamical effects in a THz quantum cascade laser. Varying the tunnel coupling across the injection barrier by changing the barrier width, different regimes are distinguished where stationary and dynamics-induced localization effects are found and discussed.

articleTitle: Predictive nonequilibrium Green's function simulation of transport in THz quantum cascade lasers
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: Efficient and predictive simulators are an essential tool for design and optimization of quantum cascade lasers (QCLs), since experimental trial and error is a time-consuming and expensive process due to the high complexity involved in the growth and processing of samples. We present a highly efficient implementation of a next-generation QCL simulator based on nonequilibrium Green's functions (NGFs), which are particularly suited for QCL simulation mainly for two reasons: (i) The operation of QCLs sensitively depends on the balance between coherent transport and scattering which NGFs can describe consistently. (ii) NGFs explicitly guarantee energy conservation.

articleTitle: Workshop co-chairs
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: Provides a listing of current society officers.

articleTitle: Workshop proceedings terahertz and mid infrared radiation: Basic research and practical applications
publicationTitle: 2009 International Workshop Terahertz and Mid Infrared Radiation: Basic Research and Practical Applications
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: infrared semiconductor based chemical sensing technologies; Mid-IR quantum cascade lasers; density-matrix theory; quantum cascade lasers; infrared photodetector; quantum well infrared photodetector; large amplitude anharmonic vibrations by monocycle intense THz pulse; electron-beam lithographed metamaterial devices; stimulated emission; inverse population; metallic photonic crystals; orotron oscillators; coherent terahertz radiation; optical rectification; spin polarized tunneling; optical spectral characteristics modeling; electrical injection of intersubband polaritons; glass transition of polymers and air-nitrogen-argon dc glow discharge plasma characterisation with terahertz time-domain spectroscopy; electro-optic detection method; electromagnetic wave diffraction; and intersubband terahertz emitters.
